entry.title: LeetCode75-790-Domino
entry.content:
动规五部曲

  1. dp数组以及下标含义
  2. 递归公式
  3. dp数组如何初始化
  4. 遍历顺序
  5. 打印dp数组

🧠 Summary of Thoughts

可以先考虑简单一些的情况: How many ways that we can cover a 2 * N board using one type of domino (1 * 2)?

每个i列的时候，都可以是前面i-1的后面加上一个竖条。或者是i-2的后面补充上一个2条横条。其实此时就转化成了fibonacci。

同理，这道题目可以化简为如下图：

这里有三个状态：

  • dp[i][0]: 前 i 列整整齐齐、完全填满（第 i 列的上下两格都被盖住了），没有任何格子凸出到第 i+1 列
  • dp[i][1]: 前 i-1 列已经填满，但第 i 列只有上面那格被填了,下面那格是空的（等着后面的瓷砖来填）
  • dp[i][2]: 前 i-1 列已经填满，但第 i 列只有下面那格被填了，上面那格是空的

🧠 Summary of Thoughts

Key Insight

We do NOT store the infinite set explicitly. Instead, we simulate it using:

  • A pointer next → tracks the smallest number that has never been removed
  • A min heap → stores numbers that were removed and later added back
  • A set → avoids duplicates in the heap

Two Methods

  1. popSmallest():
  • If heap is not empty → return the smallest element from heap
  • Otherwise → return next and increment it

  1. addBack(num):

    Only add num to heap if:

    • num < next (it was removed before) and it is not already in heap

entry.title: LeetCode75-215-Kth-Largest
entry.content:
🧠 Summary of Thoughts

Key Observations

  1. You don’t need to fully sort the array
  2. The problem is essentially:
    • Find the element at index n - k (0-based sorted order)

Common Approaches

  1. Sorting:

    • Sort the array
    • Return nums[n - k]
    • Time: O(n log n)

  2. Min Heap:

    • Maintain a min heap of size k (PriorityQueue is a min heap by default)
    • Keep only the k largest elements
    • The top of heap = answer

    Why it works:

    • Always remove the smallest → keep largest k elements
    • Time: O(n log k)
    • Space: O(k)

  3. Quickselect：

    • Partition-based (like quicksort)
    • Average: O(n)
    • Worst: O(n²)

✅ Code（Java）

  1. Sorting
  1. Min Heap

entry.title: LeetCode75-136-Single-Number
entry.content:
🧠 Summary of Thoughts

Use the bitwise XOR (^) operation to cancel out duplicate numbers.

XOR has two important properties:

  • a ^ a = 0 → same numbers cancel out
  • a ^ 0 = a → zero does not affect the result

Every number that appears twice cancels itself out. The only number left is the one that appears once. We can also reorder the ^’s left and right number to cancel the duplicate out :)

entry.title: Interview-Min-Total-Increment-for-NonDecreasing-Array
entry.content:
Problem Overview

Problem Description

You are given an array power representing the computational strength of $n$ servers. The objective is to make the array non-decreasing (where each element is greater than or equal to the previous one. i.e. $power[i] \ge power[i-1]$) with the minimum total cost.

You can choose any contiguous segment (a subarray) of servers and increase the power of every server in that segment by a value x. Find the minimum possible sum of all x values used to achieve the non-decreasing state.

Example:

Input: $power = [3,4,1,6,2]$

  • Compare 4 and 3: $4 \ge 3$, no action needed.
  • Compare 1 and 4: $1 < 4$. The difference is $3$.
    Lift the suffix by $3$. Total $x = 3$.
  • Compare 6 (now $9$) and 4: $9 \ge 4$, no action needed.
  • Compare 2 (now $5$) and 9: $5 < 9$. The difference is $4$.
    Lift the suffix by $4$. Total $x = 3 + 4 = 7$.

Output: 7

🧠 Summary of Thoughts

We don’t actually need to update the values because of Relative Difference Stability: When we lift a whole segment by x, every element in that segment moves up together.The gap between any two neighbors inside that segment remains exactly the same.Therefore, the “dips” that existed in the original array’s tail will still be the same size in the “updated” array. We just need to sum those original dip sizes.

Formula:

The minimum sum is simply the total of every “downward drop” in the original array:
$$S = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \max(0, power[i-1] - power[i])$$

✅ Code（Java）

entry.title: Interview-resourceConsumption
entry.content:
Problem Overview

The goal is to calculate the total resource consumption of tasks selected through a specific termination process in Amazon’s Elastic Container Service (ECS).

You are given an array resourceConsumption representing n tasks. You must repeat the following steps until no tasks remain:

  • Identify the Target: Find the task with the lowest resource consumption value. If multiple tasks have the same minimum value, select the one with the smallest index.
  • Record the Value: Add the value of this selected task to your running total.
  • Remove Tasks: Remove the selected task and its immediate neighbors (the tasks directly to its left and right) from the array.
  • Update Adjacency: After removal, the remaining tasks shift to become “adjacent” to each other (the gap closes).
  • Return the final sum of all selected tasks’ resource consumption values.

Example: If you have $[4, 3, 2, 1]$, you pick 1 (the minimum). Its neighbor is 2. Both are removed, leaving $[4, 3]$. Next, you pick 3 (the new minimum), and its neighbor 4 is removed. $Total = 1 + 3 = 4$.

🧠 Summary of Thoughts

ArrayList

A crucial part of this code is the Right-to-Left removal sequence:

  • Right Neighbor ($i+1$)
  • Current Task ($i$)
  • Left Neighbor ($i-1$)

By deleting the rightmost neighbor first, the code prevents “index shifting” from affecting the positions of the remaining tasks we intend to remove in the same cycle.

The use of ArrayList.remove() is clever here because it automatically shifts subsequent elements. This naturally “closes the gap”, making tasks that were previously separated become neighbors, which perfectly matches the problem’s requirements.

Doubly Linked List & Min-Priority Queue

The goal is to reduce the time complexity from $O(n^2) \rightarrow O(n \log n)$ by decoupling the “finding the minimum” step from the “removing elements” step. We use a Min-Priority Queue for efficient selection and a Doubly Linked List to maintain task adjacency in constant time (delete element).

✅ Code（Java）

entry.title: LeetCode75-199-BT-Right-Side-View
entry.content:
🧠 Summary of Thoughts

Idea

Use level-order traversal (BFS) to process the tree level by level. For each level, record the last node because it represents the node visible from the right side.

Steps

  • Use a queue to perform BFS.

  • For each level, get the number of nodes: size = queue.size().

  • Traverse all nodes in that level.

  • When visiting the last node of the level (i == size - 1), add its value to the result.

  • Push the node’s left and right children into the queue.

When to use BFS?

  1. Level by Level
  2. shortest path
  3. spread from one spot

entry.title: LeetCode75-236-LCA-BT
entry.content:
🧠 Summary of Thoughts

We find p and q traverse from bottom to top, but it’s generally believe that we can only traverse from top to bottom. But how can we traverse from bottom to top? Although we cannot traverse from bottom to top, we still can deal the order with binary tree from bottom to top. So we can think about backtrack. Remember that the order(postorder traversal) for backtrack is left -> right -> root.

  • if root == null, then return null.
  • if left node returns not NULL, then it may consist p or q. else if right node returns not NULL, then it may consist p or q. So left treeNode and right treeNode have p and q, so the current root treeNode is lowest common ancestor.
  • Then I used postorder traversal, first traverse left treeNode, and then traverse right treeNode, to get left and right recursive’s results. After that, I considered the logic of root (medium):
    • if (left != null && right != null), so the current root is LCA. Then continuously return the current root to the top.
    • if (left == null && right != null), return right. (if left doesn’t find p or q, however, right exists p or q, then continuously return right result)
    • if (left != null && right == null), return left.
    • if (left == null && right == null), return null.

✅ Code（Java）

entry.title: Interview:Assign-Next-Available-ID
entry.content:
Question:

Given an array of observed ids and a threshold, an ID is considered “active” (unavailable) if its frequency is ≥ threshold. If its frequency is < threshold, it is eligible for reuse.

You need to assign numAssignments new IDs in strictly ascending numerical order, starting from 1. During this process, you must skip any IDs that are currently “active”. Return the value of the last ID assigned.

Example: Suppose n = 7, ids = [1, 3, 2, 3, 5, 1, 3], numAssignments = 4, and threshold = 2. Output: 6

Summary of thoughts

  • We can first consider all of the integer in the array are inactive so that the output should be numAssignments. However, this is the ideal case. If there are any integer’s frequency larger than threshold, then update(add 1) the result.
  • Count frequency using HashMap, to count the occurences of each identifier
  • Use ArrayList to count which numbers are larger than or equal to threshold, which are active(unavailble to use). We can store then in a list and sort them in ascending order.
  • Imagine an ideal scenario where no IDs are occupied. If we need to assign numAssignments IDs, the last one we hand out would simply be numAssignments. Therefore, we initialize result = numAssignments.
  • If an activeId <= result, it means a number within our planned range is already taken. To compensate for this missing spot, we must push our target one step further by incrementing it (result++). If an activeId > result, it means this occupied number is completely outside our required range and doesn’t affect us. Because our list is sorted, all subsequent active IDs will also be larger, so we can safely break out of the loop early to save time.
  • Return result

entry.title: A-Gaze-Between-Diggers
entry.content:
挖掘者的一次对望

A Gaze Between Diggers

正午的阳光落在 Oval 的积雪上，并不温暖，反而衬得天地愈发寂寥。在通往 18th 图书馆的必经之路上，寒风裹挟着这个季节特有的凛冽，催促着每一个行人缩短停留的时间。

经过Thompson的门口，我看见了一只一头扎进雪地里的松鼠，

我不禁停下了脚步👣，静静地观察它。看着那只松鼠在雪地里执着地翻找，只露出了一条毛茸茸的尾巴，我突然意识到，它其实像极了每一个在寒冬里穿行的我们：在看似荒凉的现境下，不停地挖掘着曾经埋下的理想与希望。

随后它轻盈地跃上枝头，那回眸的一眼对望，仿佛是一种跨越物种的确认。它在确认这一季的口粮，而我在确认通往未来的方向。

或许它并不觉得冷，因为在那身厚实的皮毛下，正跳动着一颗对春天深信不疑的心。它守着它的树木，我奔向我的书本。我们各自行走在风雪中，却在这场不经意的偶遇里，交换了关于“坚持”的秘密。

🧠 思路总结

只要题目是“求固定长度子串的某种属性的最大/最小值”，滑动窗口通常是最优解法。

先统计第一个长度为k的窗口元音数，然后滑动窗口。每次滑动向右移动一位，减去窗口左边的字符，如果左边字符是元音，那么count--；加上新进入窗口的右端字符，如果是元音，那么count++，更新maxCount。

❗ 易错点 / 小坑

entry.title: LeetCode75-643-Max-Avg-Subarray-I
entry.content:
🧠 思路总结

什么时候用Sliding Window？

  • 当答案来自 一段连续区间，而且区间可以通过左右边界移动得到时，用滑动窗口。

为什么这道题目用Sliding Window？

  • 连续区间
  • 固定长度
  • 暴力 O(nk)， 滑动窗口 O(n)

做法：

  1. 先算第一个窗口的 sum
  2. 窗口右移：
    • 加上右边新元素
    • 减去左边移除的元素
  3. 更新最大 sum

entry.title: Leetcode75-151-Reverse-Words
entry.content:
🧠 思路总结 1 (Split)

  • 把空格切分成""，这样的话就能通过 长度 进行区分哪些是空格哪些不是
  • 所以我们使用 split(" ") 按单个空格将字符串拆分成数组
  • 连续空格会被切分成 空字符串 ""
  • 使用 StringBuilder 拼接结果，最后用 trim() 去掉多余空格

举个例子：
s = " hello world "
切完后: parts = ["", "", "hello", "", "", "world", "", ""]

🧠 思路总结 2 (Two Pointers)

  • 快指针：想要获取的元素

  • 慢指针：告诉更新在哪里（新的位置）

    思路：

    1. 整体反转
    2. 每个单词反转
    3. 快慢指针去空格

  • 流程example：
    s = " hello world "

    1. 转 char[] : “ hello world “
    2. 反转整个数组 : “ dlrow olleh “
    3. 反转每个单词 : “ world hello “
    4. 快慢指针去空格 : “world hello”

entry.title: Leetcode-101-Symmetric-Tree
entry.content:
🧠 思路总结

递归三部曲:

  1. 确定递归函数的参数和返回值
  2. 确定终止条件
  • 节点为空的情况有：
    • 左节点为空，右节点不为空，不对称，return false
    • 左不为空，右为空，不对称 return false
    • 左右都为空，对称，返回true
  • 此时已经排除掉了节点为空的情况，那么剩下的就是左右节点不为空：
    左右都不为空，比较节点数值，不相同就return false
  1. 确定单层递归的逻辑
  • 比较二叉树外侧是否对称:
    • 传入的是左节点的左孩子，右节点的右孩子。
  • 比较内侧是否对称：
    • 传入左节点的右孩子，右节点的左孩子。
      如果左右都对称就返回true，有一侧不对称就返回false。

❗ 易错点 / 小坑

遍历方式：左子树左右中，右子树右左中，所以我把这个遍历顺序也称之为“后序遍历”
